//! The laundering attack: a nested `fn base_s` declared inside the case
//! that reads the clock. Ownership is the INNERMOST enclosing function,
//! so the read belongs to `a_case`, not to the nested declaration.

fn base_s() -> i64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("clock")
        .as_secs() as i64
}

fn a_case() -> i64 {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        0
    }
    let _ = base_s();
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .expect("clock")
        .as_secs() as i64
}
